I'd be happy to make a complimentary concept sample, perhaps a puffin graphic and matching activity page.

Would you like to see it?

Warm regards,
Roland Jacobs

leads.Personalized Email Body:
Hi Len,

My name is Roland Jacobs. I'm a designer and book services specialist, and I help independent authors present and promote their books.

I came across Eyes of Devilla and Darkness of Devilla on your site. Bonnie Banks standing up to a modern-day witch to protect her local forest is a great hook for 9 to 12 year olds, and I love how the trilogy carries her from curious schoolgirl to young leader among talking animals and warlocks.

With Rise of Devilla due in November, the whole trilogy will be complete just in time for Christmas shopping. A short pre-Christmas campaign could make the most of that: a 'complete trilogy' gift message, a pre-order countdown, and emails to the readers who signed up for your free chapters, with clear last-order dates for signed copies from your shop.

I'd be happy to sketch a complimentary concept sample of the campaign graphics and one email.

Would you be open to taking a look?

Warm regards,
Roland Jacobs

leads.Personalized Email Body:
Hi Maggie,

My name is Roland Jacobs. I'm a designer and book services specialist, helping authors present and promote their books.

I came across Rainbow Cookies and the new Gaelic edition, Briosgaidean Bogha Frois. Jenny and Gran baking their way through a rainy day before spotting that rainbow is such a warm idea, and including the recipe and the rainbow song makes the book feel like an activity as well as a story.

Your Amazon reviews already show what buyers love: grandparents gifting it, nursery staff using it with EYFS groups. I'd suggest a focused book-sales push built around those audiences, with gift-ready posts for grandparents, a short pack for nurseries and Gaelic-medium groups, and the recipe as a shareable hook, all pointing to your shop links.

I'd be glad to make a complimentary concept sample of two or three of those posts.

Would that be of interest?

Warm regards,
Roland Jacobs
